messages:
alex.chen: Hey team — ACME Labs (acct: acme-123) escalated. Their Dedicated reserved GPU hours for pool `pool-ded-42` show ~4h consumed on 2026-03-05, but their token counts in our dashboard are tiny (~20k). Invoice INV-2026-042 attached. Can someone take a look?

maya.singh: @alex.chen can you paste the pool id + exact timeframe? Were they using burst capacity or reserved only? :thinking:

alex.chen: Pool: pool-ded-42. Window they reported: 2026-03-05T00:00:00Z -> 2026-03-05T12:00:00Z. Customer says they only sent a few short requests at 02:15 and 07:40. They included 3 request ids: req_01a, req_01b, req_01c. Invoice link: https://billing.redwood.ai/invoices/INV-2026-042

tom.reilly: If token burn is low but hours high, my first suspicion is idle allocation time or an allocation leak — GPU instance spun up and held for a while. We saw allocation-seconds being billed even when token throughput low. Can we repro?

priya.patel: Ask the customer for request timestamps (they gave local timestamps) and whether they used streaming/websocket. Streaming sessions can keep KV caches pinned which shows up as allocation time. If they can't, we can query traces by `acct:acme-123`.

alex.chen: They said they used only simple REST calls, no websockets. Here are the request ids/time excerpts they provided:

```
2026-03-05T02:15:18Z  req_01a  model=gpt-small  tokens_in=8 tokens_out=26
2026-03-05T07:40:03Z  req_01b  model=gpt-small  tokens_in=12 tokens_out=34
2026-03-05T07:40:10Z  req_01c  model=gpt-small  tokens_in=5 tokens_out=10
```

maya.singh: Can you grab the server-side allocation/logs for pool-ded-42 in that window? In particular look for these response headers in our access logs: `x-rw-dedicated-pool`, `x-rw-alloc-duration-ms`, `x-rw-burst-used`. If allocations were long, `x-rw-alloc-duration-ms` will be large even with low tokens.

sre-oncall: I'll start with allocation logs. Quick note: our billing pipeline debits reserved-hours at the job boundary for active allocations; bursts are accounted differently and reconciled later. There's a known race where short-lived burst allocations can be billed to reserved pool before the recon job attributes them to bursts. I'll check for that reconciliation lag.

tom.reilly: Repro steps I use locally: create a dedicated pool with min_reserved=1, then do a couple of quick requests to force spin-up and immediate teardown. Sometimes the alloc-duration recorded is large in the billing snapshot though tokens are small. Example cURL to reproduce (dev env):

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.dev.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_KEY" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Pool: pool-ded-42" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"hi"}'
```

Check response headers: `x-rw-dedicated-pool`, `x-rw-alloc-duration-ms`, `x-rw-billing-charge`, `x-rw-burst-used`.

priya.patel: I've queued a metering replay for account `acme-123` covering 2026-03-05 to 2026-03-06: job id `job-2026-03-06-002` (reason: investigation). ETA ~20m. Also opened billing ticket BT-9087 and assigned to @maya.singh and @tom.reilly.

maya.singh: If replay confirms mis-attribution we should issue a provisional SLA credit while we finish full reconciliation. Policy: provisional credit up to $500 for cases with clear pipeline bug; escalate to finance for larger amounts. I'll draft an outbound message to the customer once we have replay results. :writing_hand:

alex.chen: Customer also asked for a timeline for a credit. Can we give a provisional ETA?

sre-oncall: Let the replay finish. If trace shows allocations billed as reserved but later attributable to burst, we can mark the invoice for adjustment and apply an interim credit within 48h. Also need to confirm whether the `burst` header was present on their requests — if present, that's strong evidence.

alex.chen: I asked customer to confirm whether they saw `x-rw-burst-used` in responses (they don't have full headers saved). I also asked them to check for any long-lived streaming calls.

tom.reilly: I'll run the dev repro I mentioned and capture the metering snapshot diff. If I can recreate, we can build a regression test to prevent future billing races.

jordan_cs: Looping in for customer comms. I'll wait for confirmation before messaging ACME.

billing-bot: Billing ticket BT-9087 created. Priority: P2. Linked to invoice INV-2026-042.

alex.chen: Thanks all — I'll update the customer once `job-2026-03-06-002` finishes. If anyone finds anything urgent, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
